note.after_visit_summary: Today we looked at a mole on your left upper back that has been changing. It is asymmetric with an irregular border and a black area. Under magnification, it showed an irregular network. This mole does not look like your other moles, which are all small, round, and evenly brown. Because of these changes, I performed a shave biopsy today to check for early melanoma. The area was numbed, the mole was removed with a thin blade, and sent to the lab. No stitches were needed. Keep the bandage on for 24 hours, then wash the site gently once a day. Apply plain petroleum jelly and a fresh bandage daily until healed, which usually takes 1 to 2 weeks. Results will be ready in 7 to 10 days and will be posted to your portal. We will call you at 555-0163 with the results. If the site becomes red, hot, swollen, or drains pus, call us right away. To protect your skin, use broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 30 or higher every day on exposed skin, reapply every 2 hours when outside, and wear a wide-brimmed hat. Check your moles monthly. Since you have had blistering sunburns and many moles, you should return for a full skin check every year. Your follow-up for the biopsy site and results is scheduled for Tuesday, October 27th. Continue taking levothyroxine 75 micrograms every morning for your thyroid. You have no known medication allergies.
